request: Standardize the provisioning → enrollment detail API response flow for all delivery types in JeduShop. Goal: consistent response structure, clear rules on what is stored at provisioning vs read at request time, clean up redundant/confusing code paths.

response_shape.scope: What should the standard enrollment detail response look like? Should type-specific data be isolated inside a typed delivery_block, or should we normalize everything into a flat predictable shape?

questions.text: Enrollment detail response shape — what's the right standard?

config.question: Enrollment detail response shape — what's the right standard?
config.context: Currently: delivery_block is a union of 6 different typed Data classes. The frontend must handle 6 different shapes. quizzes and files are not in the response yet despite all types needing them.

options.label: Typed delivery_block + shared top-level fields
options.description: Keep delivery_block as a typed union (BBB/Skyroom/Moodle/SpotPlayer/InPerson/DirectDownload). Add quizzes and files as top-level siblings. Frontend reads type from product.delivery_method to know which block shape to expect.

options.label: Normalized flat envelope
options.description: All enrollments return the same top-level fields: access_url (join or LMS URL), access_label, start_date, recordings, license_key, address — null if not applicable. No union type. Frontend handles one shape always.

options.label: Typed delivery_block only — files/quizzes belong inside each block
options.description: Keep the typed delivery_block approach but move files and quizzes inside each block's definition. Each block is self-contained.

provisioning_vs_runtime.scope: Should delivery URLs (BBB join_url, Skyroom login_url) be generated at provisioning time and stored, or generated fresh at each API request?

questions.text: BBB join_url — provisioning-time vs request-time generation?

config.question: BBB join_url — provisioning-time vs request-time generation?
config.context:
Currently: ProvisionBbbEnrollmentJob stores attendee_join_url in provisioning_data. But GetEnrollmentDetailAction IGNORES that stored URL and calls BbbService to rebuild the URL fresh on every request. This is redundant duplication.

BBB join URLs are not time-limited — they are valid as long as the meeting exists. Skyroom login URLs are time-limited (TTL parameter).

options.label: Trust provisioning_data — read stored URL, no runtime API call
options.description: Action reads attendee_join_url from provisioning_data['providers']['bbb']['data']. Provisioning job is the only one that calls BbbService. Eliminates the runtime BbbService dependency from the action.

options.label: Always rebuild at request time — remove from provisioning_data
options.description: Action always calls BbbService.buildJoinUrl(). Remove storing join_url from the provisioning job — it only creates the meeting. Single responsibility per job.

options.label: Read from provisioning, regenerate only if missing
options.description: Action reads from provisioning_data first. If null (provisioning failed or not stored), falls back to rebuilding via BbbService. Resilient but more complex.

skyroom_provisioning.scope: Skyroom has no provisioning job and no SkyroomService. The enrollment detail action has a TODO stub for it. What is the right approach?

questions.text: Skyroom integration — how should it work?

config.question: Skyroom integration — how should it work?
config.context: Skyroom API: createLoginUrl(room_id, user_id, nickname, access, ttl). Login URLs are time-limited (TTL). room_id would come from details_json. No ProvisionSkyroomEnrollmentJob exists. No SkyroomService exists.

options.label: Generate login URL at request time only (no provisioning job)
options.description: Create SkyroomService. GetEnrollmentDetailAction calls it to generate a fresh time-limited URL each request. No provisioning job needed — Skyroom is stateless (no user account creation, just URL generation). Consistent with how TTL URLs should work.

options.label: Create ProvisionSkyroomEnrollmentJob — store room access in provisioning_data
options.description: Job validates room_id exists in details_json and stores the Skyroom room_id + any user metadata. Action generates fresh login URL from stored room_id. Job follows same pattern as other providers.

options.label: Skip Skyroom integration for now — leave as TODO
options.description: Keep the stub, don't implement SkyroomService yet. Focus refactor on cleaning up existing providers first.

details_json_ownership.scope: details_json on ProductDeliveryOption is set by the admin at product creation. provisioning_data on Enrollment is written by provisioning jobs. Is the current boundary between them correct, or is data in the wrong place?

questions.text: details_json vs provisioning_data — is the boundary correct?

config.question: details_json vs provisioning_data — is the boundary correct?
config.context:
Currently:
• details_json (product-level): meeting_id, attendee_password, start_date (BBB) | moodle_course_id, dates (Moodle) | course_id (SpotPlayer) | address, map_url (InPerson)
• provisioning_data (enrollment-level): bbb.data.attendee_join_url | moodle.data.course_info, moodle_user_id | spotplayer.data.license_key, player_url

Question: should any of this data move? For example — should start_date for BBB be on the enrollment (provisioning) not the product (details_json)? Should moodle course_info be fetched at request time instead of stored?

options.label: Current boundary is correct — product config in details_json, runtime results in provisioning_data
options.description: details_json = static product-level config set by admin. provisioning_data = dynamic per-enrollment results from external APIs. This is clean and the right separation. No changes needed to the schema.

options.label: Move session dates out of details_json — they belong on enrollment or a schedule model
options.description: start_date (BBB) is per-session, not per-student. But it's currently on the product option's details_json which is shared across all enrollments. Fine for now but may need a Schedule model later. Flag as tech debt.

options.label: Stop storing Moodle course_info in provisioning_data — fetch at request time
options.description: course_info (name, URL, grade, activities) can go stale. Fetch it fresh from Moodle API at request time. provisioning_data only stores moodle_user_id + moodle_course_id. Reduces provisioning_data bloat but adds latency to enrollment detail endpoint.

code_cleanup.scope: What dead code, redundant logic, or unnecessary complexity should be removed during this refactor?

questions.text: What should be cleaned up during this refactor?

config.question: What should be cleaned up during this refactor?
config.context: Looking at the current codebase, several things stand out as candidates for cleanup or removal.

options.label: Remove BbbService from GetEnrollmentDetailAction — read provisioning_data instead
options.description: Action currently injects BbbService + SettingsService just to rebuild a URL already stored in provisioning_data. If we trust provisioning_data, these dependencies disappear from the action.

options.label: Extract build*Block() private methods into dedicated resolver classes
options.description: Each delivery type gets its own resolver. Action becomes a thin orchestrator. New delivery types = new file only.

options.label: Remove raw_response from SpotPlayer provisioning_data
options.description: ProvisionSpotPlayerEnrollmentJob stores raw_response in provisioning_data. This is noise — only license_key and player_url are needed. Remove it.

options.label: Remove duplicated findEnrollment() from every provisioning job
options.description: All 4 provisioning jobs have an identical findEnrollment() private method. Move to HandlesProvisioningStatus trait.

options.label: Remove method_exists() hack in buildDirectDownloadBlock()
options.description: Currently checks method_exists($productable, 'digitalAssets') as a runtime duck-type check. Should use a proper interface or relationship that's always present.
